findings.evidence: Reductive/Over.lean:43-57 and Semisimple/Over.lean:60-76 are the same text with `reductive` replaced by `semisimple`.
findings.fix: Define one predicate, e.g. `geometricFiberwiseOver (P : ∀ (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k], ObjectProperty (FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.{u,u} k)) R H := Algebra.Smooth R H ∧ ∀ k ..., P k (baseChange H)`. Prove its API once, then make the reductive and semisimple predicates instances of it, or abbrevs of it.
findings.issue: `semisimpleCommHopfAlgPropertyOver` and its `_iff`, `smooth` and `geometricFiber` are copies of the `reductiveCommHopfAlgPropertyOver` versions with only the fibre predicate changed. This repeats a special case of a general fibrewise construction.

findings.evidence: The proofs differ only in `(reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty k).prop_of_iso` vs `(semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty k).prop_of_iso`.
findings.fix: Prove both once for the general fibrewise predicate, assuming `∀ k, (P k).IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms`, and derive the reductive and semisimple versions from it.
findings.issue: The `IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms` instance and `baseChange` (line 112) repeat Reductive/Over.lean:60-70 and :87-99 word for word. They only need the fibre property to be closed under isomorphisms.

findings.evidence: Both proofs consist of the same `smoothCommHopfAlgProperty.tensorProduct` step plus `prop_of_iso (baseChangeTensorProductIso k H K).symm`.
findings.fix: Prove a general product theorem for the fibrewise predicate, assuming the fibre property is closed under isomorphisms and under `FiniteTypeCommHopfAlgCat.tensorProduct`. Get both instances by passing in `reductiveCommHopfAlgProperty.tensorProduct` and `semisimpleCommHopfAlgProperty.tensorProduct`.
findings.issue: The new `reductiveCommHopfAlgPropertyOver.tensorProduct` and `semisimpleCommHopfAlgPropertyOver.tensorProduct` (Semisimple/Over.lean:127) are the same proof twice, differing only in which field-level `tensorProduct` lemma they call.

summary: The statements are at the right level, and `[Algebra ℚ R]` is the natural hypothesis for the descent theorem, but the semisimple relative predicate repeats the reductive one declaration by declaration instead of deriving both from one general fibrewise predicate. The repeated parts are the iso-invariance instance, `baseChange`, `tensorProduct` and the accessors.
